facts.content: Patient reports a 3-day history of watery diarrhea occurring 4 to 5 times per day.
Patient has mild intermittent abdominal pain.
Patient had 1 episode of vomiting.
Patient reports mild subjective fever.
Patient has decreased appetite but is maintaining fluid intake.
Patient reports no blood or mucus in the diarrhea.
Patient has not had recent travel or diet change and has taken no medications for symptoms.
facts.source_text: no recent travel or diet change; no meds taken for sx

facts.content: Patient has a history of asthma.
Patient uses an inhaler for asthma, name Lexapro, details unknown.
Patient has no known allergies.
Patient's father had hypertension.
Patient's father died of bowel cancer at age 62.
Acute gastroenteritis or viral diarrhea is mild with no red flags.
facts.source_text: Acute gastroenteritis/viral diarrhea – mild, no red flags

facts.content: Asthma is stable.
Advised oral rehydration with Dioralyte as needed.
Recommended a soft or bland diet including toast, crackers, mashed vegetables and to avoid dairy (except yogurt), meat, fish, and eggs until 48 hours symptom-free.
facts.source_text: Soft/bland diet (toast, crackers, mashed veg); avoid dairy (except yogurt), meat, fish, eggs until 48 h symptom-free

facts.content: Suggested yogurt or probiotics to restore gut flora.

Educated to return if diarrhea persists beyond 1 week, exceeds 6 to 8 stools per day, or if blood or mucus is present, or signs of dehydration occur, to obtain a stool sample and possibly hospitalize.
facts.source_text: Education: return if >1 wk diarrhea, >6–8 stools/day, blood/mucus, or dehydration → stool sample ± hospital

facts.content: If symptoms persist or become complicated, send stool culture and consider antibiotics based on results.
facts.source_text: If persists/complicated: send stool culture, consider abx per results

facts.content: Continue asthma inhaler as usual.
Patient appears well-hydrated and non-toxic via video consultation.
